title: Applied ML eval harness: prompt sets, model onboarding, quantization profiles, and regression triage playbook
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied-ML evaluation practices for the eval harness, prompt set creation, model onboarding, quantization profile recommendations, and regression triage. It is intended for ML Engineers, Applied ML researchers, and Platform owners responsible for model quality and release stability.

Scope: Covers: (1) eval harness usage and CI integration, (2) prompt set design and benchmark creation, (3) model onboarding checklist and guardrails, (4) quantization profile selection and validation, (5) regression detection and triage process.

1) Owner & Roles
- Document owner: Applied ML (priya-shah@redwood.ai)
- Primary teams: applied-ml, model-onboarding, runtime-performance, eng-platform
- Escalation contacts: Marcus Li (applied-ml lead), Sofia Reyes (runtime-performance)

2) Eval Harness: architecture & CI integration
Intro: The eval harness (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness) is the canonical test runner for paper-style metrics, business-level QA, and production regression detection. It runs locally, in CI, and as scheduled jobs in the evaluation cluster (k8s namespace: eval-harness-prod).
Key components:
- Runner service: pytest-based runner with pluggable metric backends (BLEU, ROUGE, ExactMatch, embedding-similarity, human-eval metadata)
- Dataset store: S3 bucket s3://redwood-evals/prompt-sets/{owner}/{suite} with manifest.json for metadata
- Config: evaluations are defined in YAML: workload, model_variants, sampling_seed, postprocessors
- Metrics store: InfluxDB + Timescale + evaluation metadata persisted to postgres for auditability

CI Integration (recommended):
1. Add a level-2 eval job in the model PR pipeline that runs the fast-smoke suite (max 30m).
2. For large model upgrades, trigger the nightly full-eval suite (can take up to 8h).
3. CI must fail the PR if any critical metric regresses beyond thresholds defined in the suite manifest.

3) Prompt sets & benchmark design
Guidelines:
- Source provenance: Each prompt must include source, author, creation_date, and a brief description of intended behavior.
- Coverage: Ensure coverage across length buckets, instruction complexity (0-3), hallucination-risk scenarios, and safety edges.
- Example ratio: For balance, recommend 60% real user-derived prompts, 30% synthetic variations, 10% adversarial probes.
- Template naming: {product-area}-{intent}-{lang}-{version} (e.g., search-rewrite-en-v1)

Benchmark manifest (required fields in manifest.json):
- suite_name (string)
- owner (team string)
- primary_metrics (list of metric names)
- pass_thresholds (map-like stringified, see example below)
- evaluation_period (daily|weekly|monthly)

Example manifest snippet (place in prompt set root):
```
{\n  "suite_name": "customer-support-short-answer-en-v2",\n  "owner": "applied-ml",\n  "primary_metrics": ["exact_match","f1","embedding_similarity"],\n  "pass_thresholds": "{\\"exact_match\\":0.72,\\"embedding_similarity\\":0.86}",\n  "evaluation_period": "daily"\n}
```

4) Model onboarding checklist (must complete before model is promoted to hosted/dedicated pools)
Pre-onboarding: estimate cost, tokenization sanity check, license review, security scan
Onboarding steps (numbered):
1. Baseline evaluation: run the model against the canonical full-eval suite for the target product area (record all metrics).
2. Latency profiling: record p50/p90/p99 generation latency at production-like batch sizes. Target p90 < 250ms for chat-small workloads; adjust based on model family.
3. Throughput testing: verify sustained tokens/sec on our serving hardware (benchmark harness: repo/eval-harness/scripts/throughput.py).
4. Quantization validation: run quantization profiles (see section 5) and compare metric deltas.
5. Safety & filter tests: execute safety prompt sets; if safety failure > 0.5% or high-severity incidents, escalation to safety team required.
6. Regression gating: compare to current production baseline; if primary metric drop > 2% absolute or 10% relative, block onboarding and follow regression triage.
7. Documentation: publish model page in confluence with model-card, quantization notes, eval-results link, and recommended deployment profiles.

Ownership & sign-off: Applied ML lead (owner) must sign-off after steps 1-6; Security and Product should be cc'd for customer-sensitive models.

5) Quantization profiles and recommended validation matrix
Purpose: Provide standardized profiles that trade accuracy for memory and latency gains while bounding quality regressions. All profiles are tested against the full-eval suite and a quantization-smoke prompt-set.
Table: profile, target precision, expected memory reduction, recommended use-case, validation delta budget
- fp16: fp16, ~1.0x memory (baseline), use for GPU-native FP16 inference; delta budget: 0.0-0.5% on primary metrics
- int8-dq: dynamic quant int8, ~2-2.5x memory reduction, low-latency CPU inference; delta budget: up to 1.5% absolute on non-safety metrics
- int8-static: static calibration int8, ~2.5x memory reduction, recommended for stable models with calibration corpus; delta budget: up to 2.5% absolute
- awq-4bit: asymmetric weight quant 4-bit, ~3.5x-4x memory reduction, recommended for cost-critical workloads; delta budget: up to 5% on non-core metrics (requires explicit product sign-off)

Calibration & validation steps for each profile:
1. Select calibration corpus: 5k prompts representative of distribution (include long-context cases).
2. Run quantize step and generate pre/post eval metrics.
3. Measure embedding drift: average cosine similarity between FP16 and quantized embeddings; recommended min similarity > 0.92 for retrieval tasks.
4. If metric deltas exceed profile budget, try per-layer fallback (mixed precision) or higher-bit profile. Document results in model-card.

6) Regression detection thresholds & triage playbook
Detection rules (automated):
- Alert if any primary metric absolute drop > 1.5% OR relative drop > 8% across the full-eval suite.
- Alert if embedding-similarity average drops > 0.03 OR pairwise cosine drift > 0.05 for top-k retrieval results.
- Safety alert: any high-severity safety incident (policy violation) triggers immediate paging to safety-oncall.

Triage steps (ordered):
1. Confirm: run the failing suite again on stable infra to rule out CI flakiness.
2. Scope: identify whether regression is model-only, quantization-induced, or infra-related (hardware, kernel, runtime). Compare metrics across model variants and quantization profiles.
3. Check data/inputs: re-run with recorded seed and request traces; verify tokenization and prompt canonicalization.
4. Rollback criteria: if production delta exceeds emergency thresholds (primary metric drop > 3% absolute or safety incidents), trigger immediate rollback to previous model.
5. Remediation: Depending on root cause: apply quantization rollback, apply prompt-prefilters, revert kernel/runtime change, or open a model-quality PR with suggested fixes and new prompt-tests.
6. Postmortem: For any regression that resulted in rollback, owner must open a postmortem within 72 hours with: timeline, impact estimate (users / requests / tokens), root cause, fix, and preventive actions.

7) Playbook runbook & commands (examples)
- Run smoke suite locally: python -m eval_harness.run --suite smoke --model path/to/model --out results.json
- Generate throughput report: ./scripts/throughput_benchmark.sh --model path/to/model --batch 8 --steps 3000
- Quantize and evaluate: python -m eval_harness.quantize --model path --profile int8-dq --calib-corpus s3://redwood-evals/calibration/corpus-v1 --out quant_results.json

8) Reporting & dashboards
- All eval runs must push summary metrics to the "applied-ml-evals" timeseries dashboard (Grafana board: team/applied-ml/evals).
- Regression alerts are sent to channel #applied-ml-regressions and create an issue in the model-onboarding board.

9) Quality guardrails (operational rules)
- Any new model that reduces average customer satisfaction proxy metric by > 1% must be held for manual review.
- Safety and privacy test suites are required for all models with customer data exposure.
- Models deployed to dedicated/private must include an audit log of eval results and signed model-card.

Appendix: Example checklist snippet to include in PR description:
- [ ] Full-eval suite run attached (link)
- [ ] Latency & throughput benchmarks attached (link)
- [ ] Quantization profiles tested and results (link)
- [ ] Safety tests passed (link)
- [ ] Owner sign-off (name + timestamp)
